summary.en: Sole trader, LLC or joint-stock company: who's liable, and what it means for you. Check local rules before registering.
summary.bs: Obrt, d.o.o. ili d.d.: ko odgovara i šta to znači za tebe. Prije registracije provjeri lokalna pravila.

concepts.youtubeQuery: sole trader vs limited company explained

en.one: A sole trader is one person running a business in their own name. The business and the owner are legally the same.
en.explain: It's the simplest and cheapest form to start: little paperwork, easy accounting. But the owner is personally liable for all business debts, which means your house, car and savings can be at risk if the business can't pay.
en.example: A hairdresser registers as an obrt. It's cheap to set up and she keeps the profits, but if she can't repay a business loan, the bank can go after her personal savings.
en.why: It's a great way to test an idea or freelance with low risk and low cost.
en.mixup: 'Small' doesn't automatically mean sole trader is best. If the business takes on debt or big contracts, limited liability may be safer.

bs.one: Sole trader (samostalni preduzetnik, obrt) je jedna osoba koja vodi posao u svoje ime. Firma i vlasnik su pravno isto.
bs.explain: To je najjednostavniji i najjeftiniji oblik za početak: malo papirologije, lako knjigovodstvo. Ali vlasnik lično odgovara za sve dugove firme, što znači da kuća, auto i ušteđevina mogu biti u riziku ako firma ne može platiti.
bs.example: Frizerka registruje obrt. Jeftino je za otvoriti i ona zadržava dobit, ali ako ne može vratiti poslovni kredit, banka može ići na njenu ličnu ušteđevinu.
bs.why: Odličan je način da se testira ideja ili radi kao frilenser uz mali rizik i mali trošak.
bs.mixup: 'Mali posao' ne znači automatski da je obrt najbolji. Ako se firma zadužuje ili ima velike ugovore, ograničena odgovornost može biti sigurnija.

en.one: Limited liability means the owners can only lose what they put into the company, not their personal belongings.
en.explain: The company is a separate 'legal person': it owns things, signs contracts and has its own debts. If it goes bust, creditors can take the company's assets but usually not the owners' houses or savings.
en.example: Two friends put 10,000 KM into a d.o.o. It fails owing 50,000 KM. They lose their 10,000 KM, but the remaining debt isn't theirs personally.
en.why: It lets people take business risks without risking their whole life, which is why most growing firms use it.
en.mixup: It isn't total protection. If owners sign personal guarantees for loans or commit fraud, they can still be personally liable.

bs.one: Limited liability (ograničena odgovornost) znači da vlasnici mogu izgubiti samo ono što su uložili u firmu, a ne svoju ličnu imovinu.
bs.explain: Firma je posebno 'pravno lice': posjeduje stvari, potpisuje ugovore i ima svoje dugove. Ako propadne, povjerioci mogu uzeti imovinu firme, ali obično ne kuće ili ušteđevinu vlasnika.
bs.example: Dvoje prijatelja uloži 10.000 KM u d.o.o. Firma propadne s dugom od 50.000 KM. Izgube svojih 10.000 KM, ali ostatak duga nije njihov lični.
bs.why: Omogućava ljudima da preuzmu poslovni rizik bez rizikovanja cijelog života, zato je koristi većina firmi koje rastu.
bs.mixup: Nije potpuna zaštita. Ako vlasnici potpišu lične garancije za kredite ili počine prevaru, i dalje mogu lično odgovarati.

concepts.youtubeQuery: what is an LLC limited company explained

en.one: An LLC (d.o.o., GmbH, Ltd) is the most common company form for small and medium businesses.
en.explain: It's owned by one or more members, has limited liability, and needs a founding act, a small starting capital, registration in the court register and a director. It keeps double-entry books and pays profit tax; owners get money through salary or dividends.
en.example: A web agency with three partners registers as a d.o.o. Each owns a share, one is the director, and the company signs all client contracts.
en.why: It combines protection for the owners with a professional image for banks and big clients.
en.mixup: The company's money isn't the owner's money. Taking cash out without a proper salary, dividend or loan agreement can cause tax and legal trouble.

bs.one: LLC (društvo s ograničenom odgovornošću, d.o.o.) je najčešći oblik firme za mala i srednja preduzeća.
bs.explain: Posjeduje ga jedan ili više članova, ima ograničenu odgovornost i traži osnivački akt, mali početni kapital, upis u sudski registar i direktora. Vodi dvojno knjigovodstvo i plaća porez na dobit; vlasnici dobijaju novac kroz platu ili dividendu.
bs.example: Web agencija s tri partnera registruje se kao d.o.o. Svako ima udio, jedan je direktor, a firma potpisuje sve ugovore s klijentima.
bs.why: Spaja zaštitu vlasnika s profesionalnim imidžom pred bankama i velikim klijentima.
bs.mixup: Novac firme nije novac vlasnika. Podizanje gotovine bez prave plate, dividende ili ugovora o zajmu može izazvati porezne i pravne probleme.

concepts.youtubeQuery: joint stock company vs private limited company explained

en.one: A joint-stock company (d.d., AG, plc) divides its ownership into shares that can be sold to many investors, sometimes on a stock exchange.
en.explain: It needs more starting capital and stricter rules: a supervisory board, audited accounts and public reporting. In return, it can raise large amounts of money from many shareholders.
en.example: A big telecom or a bank is usually a d.d. Its shares are traded on the Sarajevo or Banja Luka stock exchange.
en.why: It's the form that lets companies grow very large by pooling money from thousands of owners.
en.mixup: Most start-ups don't need it. It's expensive to run, and an LLC can also take in investors.

bs.one: Joint-stock company (dioničko društvo, d.d.) dijeli vlasništvo na dionice koje se mogu prodati mnogim investitorima, ponekad na berzi.
bs.explain: Traži više početnog kapitala i strožija pravila: nadzorni odbor, revidirane izvještaje i javno izvještavanje. Zauzvrat, može prikupiti velike iznose od mnogo dioničara.
bs.example: Veliki telekom ili banka su obično d.d. Njihovim dionicama se trguje na Sarajevskoj ili Banjalučkoj berzi.
bs.why: To je oblik koji firmama omogućava da postanu vrlo velike udruživanjem novca hiljada vlasnika.
bs.mixup: Većini start-upa ne treba. Skup je za vođenje, a i d.o.o. može primiti investitore.

en.one: A shareholder (or founders') agreement is a private contract between co-owners about how they run the company and handle tough situations.
en.explain: It covers who decides what, how profits are shared, what happens if someone wants to leave, dies or stops working, and how shares can be sold. It's best written at the start, while everyone still gets along.
en.example: Three founders agree that anyone who leaves in the first two years must sell their shares back at the original price. When one leaves after 8 months, there's no fight.
en.why: Most start-up breakups are about people, not products. A clear agreement prevents expensive fights.
en.mixup: The founding act registered with the court isn't enough. It covers the basics, not the 'what if' situations between owners.

bs.one: Ugovor među osnivačima (ili dioničarima) je privatni ugovor između suvlasnika o tome kako vode firmu i rješavaju teške situacije.
bs.explain: Pokriva ko odlučuje o čemu, kako se dijeli dobit, šta se dešava ako neko želi otići, umre ili prestane raditi, i kako se udjeli mogu prodati. Najbolje ga je napisati na početku, dok se svi još slažu.
bs.example: Tri osnivača se dogovore da svako ko ode u prve dvije godine mora prodati udio nazad po početnoj cijeni. Kad jedan ode nakon 8 mjeseci, nema svađe.
bs.why: Većina razlaza u start-upima je zbog ljudi, a ne proizvoda. Jasan ugovor sprečava skupe svađe.
bs.mixup: Osnivački akt registrovan na sudu nije dovoljan. Pokriva osnove, a ne situacije 'šta ako' između vlasnika.

concepts.youtubeQuery: how to register a business steps

en.one: Registering a business makes it legally exist, so it can sign contracts, open a bank account, invoice and pay taxes.
en.explain: Typical steps: choose the legal form and name, prepare founding documents, pay in the starting capital if needed, register with the court or municipality, get a tax number (and VAT number if required), open a bank account, and register employees for social insurance. In BiH the steps differ between FBiH, RS and Brčko.
en.example: A new d.o.o. in Sarajevo goes through notary, court register, tax administration and bank before it can send its first invoice.
en.why: Working without registering can bring fines and leaves you without legal protection.
en.mixup: Registration isn't the last step. Some activities also need a permit or licence, like food, health or transport.

bs.one: Registracija firme je čini pravno postojećom, pa može potpisivati ugovore, otvoriti račun, izdavati fakture i plaćati porez.
bs.explain: Tipični koraci: izaberi pravni oblik i naziv, pripremi osnivačke dokumente, uplati početni kapital ako je potreban, registruj se na sudu ili u općini, dobij porezni broj (i PDV broj ako treba), otvori račun u banci i prijavi radnike na socijalno osiguranje. U BiH se koraci razlikuju između FBiH, RS i Brčkog.
bs.example: Novi d.o.o. u Sarajevu prolazi kroz notara, sudski registar, poreznu upravu i banku prije nego može poslati prvu fakturu.
bs.why: Rad bez registracije može donijeti kazne i ostavlja te bez pravne zaštite.
bs.mixup: Registracija nije zadnji korak. Neke djelatnosti traže i dozvolu ili licencu, npr. hrana, zdravstvo ili prevoz.

q.en: An LLC with 10,000 KM of capital fails owing 50,000 KM. Who pays the remaining debt?
q.bs: D.o.o. s kapitalom od 10.000 KM propadne s dugom od 50.000 KM. Ko plaća ostatak duga?

options.en: Usually nobody personally, owners lose only their investment
options.bs: Obično niko lično, vlasnici gube samo ulog

explain.en: That's limited liability, unless owners signed personal guarantees.
explain.bs: To je ograničena odgovornost, osim ako vlasnici nisu potpisali lične garancije.

q.en: What is the main downside of being a sole trader?

explain.en: The owner and the business are legally the same, so personal assets are at risk.
explain.bs: Vlasnik i firma su pravno isto, pa je lična imovina u riziku.

q.en: When is the best time to write a founders' agreement?
q.bs: Kada je najbolje napisati ugovor među osnivačima?

options.en: When a founder wants to leave
options.bs: Kad neko od osnivača želi otići

options.en: At the start, while everyone gets along
options.bs: Na početku, dok se svi slažu

explain.en: Agreeing on the 'what ifs' is much easier before there's a conflict.
explain.bs: Dogovor o situacijama 'šta ako' je mnogo lakši prije sukoba.

q.en: Which form usually suits a company that wants to list shares on a stock exchange?
q.bs: Koji oblik obično odgovara firmi koja želi dionice na berzi?

explain.en: A d.d. divides ownership into shares that can be traded publicly.
explain.bs: D.d. dijeli vlasništvo na dionice kojima se može javno trgovati.
